messages.content: United changed the Sunday return. It now leaves Seattle at 3:05 and does not get into O'Hare until 10:37 p.m. Can you check whether there is an earlier nonstop with three seats, and compare the full cost before changing anything?

I found two earlier nonstop options for Sunday, November 30. United 2216 still operates at 1:20 p.m., arriving ORD at 7:18 p.m., but moving all three travelers back to it would add $684 total. Alaska 328 departs SEA at 11:45 a.m. and arrives ORD at 5:52 p.m.; three economy seats are available for $2,109 total as a new booking. Your retimed United itinerary remains confirmed at no additional charge.
So the United option is $684 on top of what we already paid, not $684 total?

Correct. United is quoting a $228 fare difference per traveler, or $684 total, to move Marcus, Daniel, and Owen to the 1:20 p.m. flight. The existing tickets retain their current value; this would be an additional charge.
What time would we realistically get home with each one? We are in Chicago, and we will have one checked bag.

For the 1:20 p.m. United flight, landing at 7:18 p.m., allow about 35 to 50 minutes to deplane and collect the bag, then roughly 35 to 55 minutes for the drive home. A realistic home arrival is 8:30 to 9:00 p.m. The retimed flight lands at 10:37 p.m.; with the same allowances, expect to reach home around 11:50 p.m. to 12:20 a.m. Monday.
And Alaska would put us home around 7:00?

Approximately. With its 5:52 p.m. arrival, baggage claim and the drive from O'Hare put you home around 7:05 to 7:35 p.m. However, buying Alaska and canceling the United return would cost substantially more than paying United's $684 fare difference, and the remaining United ticket value may be issued as credits rather than refunded.
Check seats on the 1:20 United flight. I do not want to pay that and then find out we are scattered.
There are three adjacent standard economy seats available: 24A, 24B, and 24C. United is not charging an additional seat-selection fee for those seats. The $684 total fare difference is unchanged.
Is there anything between the 1:20 and the changed flight that costs less?

There is a 2:35 p.m. American nonstop arriving ORD at 8:42 p.m. Three seats are available, but a new booking would be $1,836 total. After accounting for the likely United flight credits, it is not a cleaner or cheaper solution than moving back to United 2216. No other nonstop in that window currently has three economy seats for less.
Then move all three of us back to the 1:20 United flight and take 24A through C. Keep everything else as it is.

Before I submit, the additional charge is $684 total to the payment method on file. United 2216 departs SEA Sunday, November 30, at 1:20 p.m. and arrives ORD at 7:18 p.m. Seats will be 24A, 24B, and 24C, with the checked bag allowance preserved. The Wednesday American outbound and Coast Gateway Hotel reservation will not change. Shall I complete it?

Completed. United confirmation H7LM2Q now has Marcus, Daniel, and Owen on United 2216 Sunday, November 30, departing SEA at 1:20 p.m. and arriving ORD at 7:18 p.m. Seats 24A, 24B, and 24C are assigned, and the checked bag allowance remains in place. The additional charge was $684 total. Plan on reaching home around 8:30 to 9:00 p.m. The Wednesday outbound on American 2367 and Coast Gateway Hotel reservation CGH-730194 are unchanged.
